# Supply Chain Pulse: San Jose Component Shortages Drive Most Late Cost

**San Jose HQ's component shortages are the main problem.** San Jose accounts for 83 of 119 late orders (70%) and $3.23M of $4.40M late cost (73%). Its OTIF is 59.7%, against a network figure of 71.7%. Component shortage is the top cause network-wide: 67 orders and $2.73M (62% of late cost). Two other risks need action soon: Austin's Stepper LIT2-1 (51% failure probability) and 18 deviating component lots.

## Evidence

| Plant | OTIF % | Late $ | Operating rate % | Material loss | Worst component (shortfall days) | Max tool failure prob |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| San Jose HQ | 59.7 | 3,233,345 | 63.9 | 47.9 | Vision Camera Module (50.7) | 0.035 |
| Dresden Fab | 82.3 | 423,050 | 86.2 | 9.3 | Reflectance Detector Array (38.9) | 0.033 |
| Austin Fab | 81.3 | 385,930 | 79.0 | 21.4 | Vacuum Chamber (38.9) | **0.506** |
| Penang Assembly | 79.5 | 351,920 | 84.8 | 14.7 | UV Laser Module (20.4) | 0.030 |
| Singapore Hub | 96.3 | 10,500 | 87.2 | 6.7 | Wafer Handler (39.7) | 0.350 |

**Why this matters:**
- **Components are the binding constraint at all five plants.** San Jose is worst, with 6 critical components. The Vision Camera Module has 5.3 days of cover against a 56-day lead time from Coherent Corp.
- **Six categories are single-sourced**, including Optics Modules and Sub-assemblies. This amplifies any shortage.
- **Lot quality is spreading downstream.** 18 of 107 lots are deviating, exposing 161 orders worth $132.4M. Lot CL-201-04 (Vacuum Chamber, TRUMPF) alone reached 28 systems across 6 customers.

**Relationships followed:**
- Sales Order → Plant → Component → Supplier
- System Serial -has part-> Component Lot
- System Serial -shipped on-> Sales Order -placed by-> Customer

## Actions

1. **Expedite Vision Camera Module supply.** Ask Coherent Corp for an expedited or partial receipt, and qualify a second source. Run the "Shortage — Vision Camera Module" preset (50 days, severity 0.35) to size the backlog.
2. **Schedule preventive maintenance on Stepper LIT2-1 now.** Its work center is about 30% of Austin's capacity, and it shows a 51% failure risk within 48h plus anomalous vibration. Run the 14-day tool-failure preset. Also review Robotic Assembly Cell ASM4-1 in Singapore (35% failure probability).
3. **Contain CL-201-04.** Trace affected serials to their customers, and run the TRUMPF supplier-hold preset (21 days) before notifying those customers.
4. **Start dual-sourcing the six single-source categories.** Prioritize categories feeding San Jose's critical components.

3. **Re-inspect CL-701-04.** Its 52% not-first-pass rate suggests a defect that incoming inspection missed.

# Equipment Risk: Two Tools Stand Out

**Two tools are far outside the fleet norm.** Stepper LIT2-1 at Austin Fab has a 50.6% chance of failing in the next 48 hours and is the only tool with an active anomaly flag. Robotic Assembly Cell ASM4-1 at Singapore Hub is at 35.0%, yet it carries no anomaly flag. Every other tool is at or below 3.5%.

## Evidence (readings dated 2025-09-30)

| Equipment | Plant | Criticality | 48h failure prob | Vibration (mm/s) | Anomaly flag | Plant open orders |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stepper LIT2-1 | Austin Fab (PLT-2000) | B | **0.5055** | **4.866** | **TRUE** | 1 (64 orders, $54.6M) |
| Robotic Assembly Cell ASM4-1 | Singapore Hub (PLT-4000) | B | **0.3497** | **4.157** | FALSE | 0 (27 orders, $22.6M) |
| Next highest: CVD DEPO-1 / PVD DEP2-2 | San Jose / Austin | B / C | 0.0347 | 1.721 / 1.286 | FALSE | 1 / 1 |

**Why it matters**

- **Clear separation from the fleet.** Both outliers run at roughly 2–2.5× the vibration of the other 18 tools, which range from 1.124 to 2.182 mm/s. High vibration plausibly explains the elevated failure probability.
- **Austin is the immediate exposure.** LIT2-1 sits in Austin's Lithography work center, and Austin has 1 open order.
- **Singapore suggests a monitoring gap.** ASM4-1 at 35% risk with no anomaly flag implies the flag logic or threshold is missing real risk.
- **Singapore has room to act.** With 0 open orders, a maintenance window there carries no current order exposure.

**Relationships followed:** Equipment -located at-> Plant -fulfils-> Sales Order, used to roll up plant order count, order value and open orders. No governed definition was included in the facts.

## Actions

1. **Inspect Stepper LIT2-1 within 48 hours.** Check bearings, stage and isolation mounts, and confirm whether Austin's open order depends on its lithography capacity.
2. **Prepare a fallback for Austin lithography.** Plan contingency capacity, for example San Jose's Stepper LITHO-1 (3.3% risk), in case LIT2-1 has to come down.
3. **Service ASM4-1 now.** Singapore has no open orders, so downtime is cheapest today.
4. **Review the anomaly-flag rules.** Find out why ASM4-1 was not flagged. A practical fix is to flag any tool above about 4 mm/s vibration or above about 10–20% failure probability, regardless of the current flag logic.

# SN-1001-01031: Shipped System Contains a Rejected Component Lot

**Direct answer:** On the surface, SN-1001-01031 looks clean. It passed final test, had 0 rework hours and shipped on time (OTIF) to Infineon Technologies on SO-4500103, worth $1,296,000. The concern is that its genealogy includes **2 deviating component lots**, and one of them was **Rejected** at inspection. A rejected lot inside a shipped, passed system points to either a containment escape or a genealogy data error. Either way, it needs to be resolved quickly.

**Relationships followed:** System Serial -has part-> Component Lot -supplied by-> Supplier; System Serial -shipped on-> Sales Order -placed by-> Customer; System Serial -built at-> Plant (Austin Fab, 2000).

| Lot | Supplier | Component | Inspection | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CL-102-01 | Aerotech Inc | Precision Motion Stage | **Rejected** | Vacuum seal leak rate high | SAP |
| CL-103-04 | Festo AG | Control Electronics Cabinet | Accepted with deviation | Surface contamination on optics | DEMO |
| CL-100-02 | Hamamatsu Photonics | Broadband Light Source | Accepted | none | SAP |
| CL-101-03 | Teledyne DALSA | High-Res CCD Array | Accepted | none | SAP |

**Why it stands out**
- **Rejected lot in a shipped system.** A rejected lot should have been blocked, yet the system shows no rework hours. A vacuum seal leak can be latent and may not appear at final test.
- **Data inconsistency on the Festo lot.** An "optics contamination" note is recorded against an electronics cabinet. The lot is also sourced from DEMO rather than SAP, so it is less reliable.

**Actions**
1. **Verify the genealogy.** Have Austin Fab confirm whether CL-102-01 stages were physically installed in this serial or whether the link is a recording error.
2. **Assess field risk if installed.** Work with Infineon service to schedule a vacuum leak-rate check on the motion stage. Prepare a proactive notification given the $1.3M system.
3. **Run a containment sweep.** Find every other serial linked through *has part* to CL-102-01, and open a SCAR with Aerotech.
4. **Correct the Festo record.** Fix the CL-103-04 component/deviation mismatch and reconcile the DEMO-sourced data with SAP.
